title: [human] schnorr48 reference: derive_keypair returns different pubkeys for the same seed at different call sites in one process
description: Blocking the gcp_slot_claim vector generation (nwjl.5). Reproduced in the generator process: main() calls derive_keypair(bytes(range(0x41,0x61))) -> pub 78f58a98c28ee570..., while sign_claim() calls derive_keypair(bytes(range(0x41,0x61))) with the IDENTICAL seed bytes (hex printed at both sites, same function object id, same module file /home/mark/.../python/src/lichen/crypto/schnorr48.py) -> pub adc14011f82d1c56.... derive_keypair is pure (sha512 + clamp + scalarmult_base, no state in the file) yet behaves as if the input or the binding differs per call site. A standalone python3 -c process derives adc14011 deterministically (3 calls equal). The generator's self-check correctly refuses to emit vectors whose signatures do not self-verify, so nothing invalid lands — but the anomaly needs crypto-owner eyes: is there hidden state in the reference schnorr48/nacl binding, or a second lichen.crypto.schnorr48 module instance (dual sys.path import)? Debug instrumentation was in place at capture time (derive_fn id identical at both sites).
